frame: Bench frame: +x to the right seen from the front of the bench, +y up, +z toward the viewer. Main gear (a left leg, wheel outboard) on the left, nose gear on the right. Tires stand on y = 0.
note: anchor = where the label and fly-to point sit on the built-in gear bench (web/app/models/gear.js).

parts.name: Gear attach fittings
parts.description: Where the gear transitions into the airplane's structure. The bolts are checked for security, and the skin and structure around them for wrinkles, damage and corrosion.

parts.name: Spring-steel gear leg
parts.description: A flexible spring-steel strut. It takes the impact of landing and returns it to the airframe at a rate that is not harmful; it is checked for distortion, cracks and corrosion.

parts.name: Main wheel
parts.description: A split wheel: two halves held together by tie bolts, with the valve stem on the outboard half. Checked for cracks, flaked paint and signs of overheating.

parts.name: Axle nut and wheel bearings
parts.description: Tapered roller bearings behind the hub cap, held by the axle nut. A loose nut lets the wheel move and the bearing cups spin; an over-tight one keeps the bearing from carrying the load properly.

parts.name: Main tire
parts.description: Checked for inflation, tread wear and condition, and sidewall condition. The correct pressure comes from the aircraft manufacturer's data, not from the tire's sidewall or how it looks.

sources.section: Tire Inspection on the Aircraft; Inflation

parts.name: Brake disc
parts.description: The disc turns with the wheel and is squeezed by the caliper's linings. It must not be warped, and its surface treatment must not be damaged.

parts.name: Brake caliper and linings
parts.description: The caliper holds the brake linings against the disc. Lining wear is checked against the manufacturer's limits, on many brakes with a built-in wear indicator pin, along with leaks and bolt security.

sources.section: Brake Inspection and Service; Lining Wear

parts.name: Brake line
parts.description: The hydraulic line from the master cylinder runs down the gear leg to the caliper. It must be secure, dry and free of leaks, abrasion and deep cracking.

parts.name: Nose gear shock strut
parts.description: An air-and-oil (oleo) strut: hydraulic fluid and compressed air or nitrogen absorb the landing loads. Inspected for fluid level, leaks at the packing gland, a clean exposed piston, and the extension the manufacturer specifies.

sources.topic: shock absorbing devices: oleo fluid level

parts.name: Torque links
parts.description: Two hinged links between the strut cylinder and the piston. They let the piston slide but keep it from turning, so the wheel stays aligned. Checked for cracks, secure fasteners and minimal free play.

parts.name: Shimmy damper
parts.description: A small damper on the nose gear that damps oscillations of the nose wheel. Checked for secure attachment and, on hydraulic types, for leaks; some types use an elastomer instead of fluid.

parts.name: Nose tire
parts.description: The nose wheel and tire in their fork. Same tire and wheel checks as the mains; the fork is checked for cracks and secure fasteners.
